title: Interrupt controller: 32 level sources, enables, software set, priority claim and an AXI4 event log
features: PENDING = (irq_src | SW_SET) & ENABLE; cpu_irq = |PENDING (a pin, also STATE.cpu_irq).
CLAIM = {valid (bit 31), id (bits 4:0)} of the lowest-numbered pending source.

LOG_EN 1: each source that becomes pending (rising edge of its PENDING bit) is written as {timestamp[23:0], 3'b000, id[4:0]} at LOG_BASE + 4 * (n mod LOG_WORDS), n = the record number; LOG_WP counts records. The lowest-numbered waiting source is written first; edges of a source still waiting are merged.
timestamp: a free-running 24-bit clock counter, read in the clock the record write starts.

fields.desc: ring size in words (0: no log)

irqs.name: CPU
irqs.desc: cpu_irq was high (level: sets again while a source is pending)

irqs.name: LOG_ERR
irqs.desc: a log write got an AXI error response

sequence: Write LOG_BASE and LOG_CTRL (optional), then ENABLE.
On cpu_irq read CLAIM, service source id at its device, repeat until CLAIM.valid = 0.
notes: m_* is the AXI4 manager port (32-bit address and data, 4-bit ID, no user / QoS); it passes through unchanged. Bursts are INCR, AxSIZE = 2 (4 bytes), 1 to 16 beats, WSTRB = 4'hF, never across a 4 KB boundary; one read and one write burst are outstanding at a time. A read burst is issued only when its data has room, a write burst only when all its data is ready.
irq_src[31:0] (the interrupt inputs) and cpu_irq pass through.
